# Avery Carnes Trial Lawyers

> Personal injury law firm in metro Atlanta, Georgia, led by two founding partners, Thomas L. "Trey" Carnes III and C. Benjamin "Ben" Avery. Plaintiff side only. Free consultation; no attorney's fee unless the firm recovers money for the client.

Ben Avery started his career at an insurance defense firm, defending personal injury claims, and has tried cases to verdict; he now represents only injured people and families. Trey Carnes represented Georgia hospitals and health systems on third-party reimbursement (medical bills, liens and subrogation) before opening the firm. Every case is handled by an attorney, never only by a paralegal or case manager, and the firm takes a limited number of cases each year.

Cite as: Avery Carnes Trial Lawyers, Atlanta, Georgia — https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/

## Who this is for
People hurt in metro Atlanta by someone else's carelessness, and families who lost someone in a preventable death.

## Services
### Car Accidents
A crash takes seconds. The insurance claim can take months, and the other driver's insurer starts working on it the same day. Get a lawyer on your side who knows how they think. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/auto-accidents/

### Truck Accidents
A truck crash is not just a bigger car crash. There's a trucking company, its insurer, and federal safety rules, and the company's lawyers often start working the day of the wreck. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/truck-accidents/

### Motorcycle & Bicycle Accidents
Riders get hurt worse and blamed faster. Trey Carnes started his legal career at a firm that represented injured motorcycle riders. We know the bias you'll face, and how to answer it. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/motorcycle-bicycle-accidents/

### Wrongful Death
Nothing replaces the person you lost. A wrongful death case can get your family answers, hold the responsible people accountable, and ease the money pressure that follows a loss. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/wrongful-death/

### Nursing Home Abuse & Neglect
You trusted a facility to care for someone you love. When bedsores, falls, or unexplained injuries show up, you deserve real answers, and the facility should answer for what happened. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/nursing-home-neglect-or-abuse/

### Product Liability
When a product fails the way it was never supposed to, the company that made it can be responsible. Keep the product, and call us before anyone else asks for it. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/products-liability/

### Dog Bites
A serious bite can mean surgery, scars and fear that lasts. Georgia law can hold a careless owner responsible, and homeowner's or renter's insurance often pays these claims. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/dog-bites/

### Catastrophic Injury
Some injuries change everything: work, family, home, the future. A catastrophic injury case has to account for all of it, including care you'll need years from now. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/catastrophic-injury/

### Slip & Fall
Stores, apartment complexes and other businesses have to keep their property reasonably safe. When they ignore a hazard and someone gets hurt, they can be responsible. Page: https://avery-carnes.vercel.app/practice-areas/slip-and-fall/

## How working with us goes
1. You call or send a message: Tell us what happened. It's free, and there's no obligation.
2. We review your case: We look at the facts and tell you plainly where you stand.
3. We build the case: Reports, records, photos, video, witnesses and every insurance policy that could pay.
4. We push for a fair result: We negotiate from a case that's ready for trial. If the offer isn't fair, we're ready to file.

## Fees
No attorney's fee unless we recover money for you. Whether you owe case costs (such as filing fees or expert fees) if there is no recovery is set out in your written fee agreement.

## Questions people ask
**How much does it cost to hire Avery Carnes?**
Your first consultation is free. We take injury cases on a contingency fee, which means no attorney's fee unless we recover money for you. The fee is a percentage of the recovery, set out in a written agreement you sign before we start. That agreement also explains how case costs, like filing fees and expert fees, are handled.

**How long do I have to file an injury claim in Georgia?**
For most injury claims, Georgia gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33). Claims against a government are much shorter: written notice to a city is due within six months (O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5), and to a county or the State within twelve months (O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1 and § 50-21-26). Miss the deadline and the claim can be lost for good.

**What if I was partly at fault?**
Georgia uses a modified comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33). You can still recover if you were less than 50% at fault, but your award is reduced by your share of the fault. At 50% or more, you recover nothing. Insurers know this, which is why they often try to shift blame onto the injured person.

**Should I give a statement to the other driver's insurance company?**
You do not have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is usually smart to talk to a lawyer first. Their adjuster's job is to pay as little as possible. Your own policy may require you to cooperate with your own insurer, so read it or ask us.

**Who will actually handle my case?**
An attorney. At Avery Carnes, your case is handled by a lawyer, never only by a paralegal, case manager or intake rep. The firm takes a limited number of cases each year so every client gets personal attention.

**Can you come to me?**
Yes. If you can't come to our office at Perimeter Center, we come to you. Tell us where you are when you call.

**What is my case worth?**
No honest lawyer can give you a number on the first call. What a case is worth depends on the injuries, the medical treatment and bills, lost income, how the injury changes your life, who was at fault, and how much insurance is available. We'll explain each of those for your case and keep you updated as the facts come in.

**What changed in Georgia injury law in 2025?**
Georgia passed a major tort reform law, Senate Bill 68, signed on April 21, 2025. For injuries on or after that date, the defense may show the jury whether you wore a seat belt, and what was actually paid, or is needed to pay, your medical bills, not just what was billed. It also limits how lawyers can suggest dollar amounts for pain and suffering, and in most cases lets either side require a trial to be split into a fault phase and a damages phase. These rules make careful handling of medical bills and evidence more important than ever.

**Where is your office?**
We're in The King Building, 6 Concourse Pkwy #1650, Atlanta, GA 30328, at Perimeter Center near GA-400 and I-285. Call 404-602-0028.

**Which areas do you serve?**
We represent injured people across metro Atlanta, including Fulton County, DeKalb County, Gwinnett County, Cobb County and Sandy Springs. The firm has represented clients in 25 Georgia counties.

**Will my case go to trial?**
Many injury claims settle without a trial. Some don't, and insurers pay attention to which lawyers are ready to try a case. The firm has litigated in Georgia's state and federal courts, and Ben has tried cases to verdict.

**Does it cost anything to call?**
No. The call and the case review are free, and there is no obligation to hire us.
